message.content:
{
  "decision": "REVISE",
  "issues": [
    {
      "issue_id": "ISS-01-primase-pol-alpha-conflation",
      "severity": "blocker",
      "description": "The enzyme object 'primase' is labeled 'Primase / Pol alpha'. In the standard teaching model, primase (an RNA polymerase) synthesizes the RNA primer, while Pol α (DNA polymerase alpha) extends the primer with a short DNA segment before handoff to Pol ε or Pol δ. Conflating them into one labeled object misrepresents the priming step and the Pol α role supported by F5.",
      "root_cause_stage": "SCENE_IR",
      "target_objects": ["primase"],
      "target_events": ["event_2_priming", "event_4_two_modes"],
      "repair_scope": "Separate the primase and Pol α labels/roles. Either use a single 'Primase' label for RNA primer synthesis only, or add a distinct short-DNA synthesis step for Pol α; do not label one enzyme as both.",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Primase object label does not claim to be Pol α.",
        "If Pol α is shown, it is a distinct step/object that extends the RNA primer with DNA before polymerase handoff.",
        "Event captions for priming and fragment synthesis do not attribute Pol α activity to primase."
      ]
    },
    {
      "issue_id": "ISS-02-lagging-fragment-extend-direction-conflict",
      "severity": "blocker",
      "description": "Fragment_1 and fragment_2 are extended with the growing end moving left (negative x), consistent with constraint growth_fragment_1/2 unit_vector [-1,0,0]. However, the objects' endpoint_labels declare the 3' end at the right-side 'end' anchor, and the extension moves the right-side 'end' anchor leftward. Under the standard antiparallel model, lagging-strand DNA synthesis proceeds 5'→3' away from the fork on the left side; the growing 3' end should move leftward, but the fragment's 3' label is on the right terminus, creating an internal polarity/geometry inconsistency unless the fragment is drawn with its 5' end on the right.",
      "root_cause_stage": "SCENE_IR",
      "target_objects": ["fragment_1", "fragment_2", "gap_fill"],
      "target_events": ["event_4_two_modes", "event_5_maturation"],
      "repair_scope": "Reconcile fragment endpoint labels with the shown growth direction and template polarity. Either relabel the growing end as 3' and place it on the left, or flip the fragment geometry so the 3' end is the leftward-growing terminus.",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "For each lagging nascent fragment, the anchor labeled 3' coincides with the growing end that actually moves during extension.",
        "Fragment extension direction remains opposite to leading-strand extension and consistent with antiparallel template polarity.",
        "The 5'→3' synthesis direction is unambiguously readable from labels and motion."
      ]
    },
    {
      "issue_id": "ISS-03-maturation-connect-gapfill-fragment1",
      "severity": "major",
      "description": "The maturation step connects gap_fill 'end' anchor to fragment_1 'start' anchor to seal a nick. However, fragment_1 was previously extended leftward from its start anchor, so its 'start' anchor is the rightmost (origin) end, while gap_fill is extended from its start at x≈-0.6 to its end at x≈-1.2. The adjacent endpoints for ligation should be gap_fill end and fragment_1's leftward growing end, not fragment_1 start. The declared connection may join non-adjacent endpoints, creating a topology error.",
      "root_cause_stage": "SCENE_IR",
      "target_objects": ["gap_fill", "fragment_1", "ligase"],
      "target_events": ["event_5_maturation"],
      "repair_scope": "Correct the connect target anchors so ligation joins the actual adjacent nick between the filled gap and the 3' end of fragment_1 (or the appropriate downstream fragment end), and update the sealed_actual_nick constraint accordingly.",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "The ligation connection uses geometrically adjacent endpoints (distance within tolerance at the time of connection).",
        "The connected ends correspond to the nick expected after RNA removal and gap fill.",
        "Postcondition relation sealed_nick refers to the corrected adjacent pair."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "notes": [
    "Static state-transition checks passed, but those checks do not validate biological labels or endpoint polarity; the issues above are scientific IR problems.",
    "Event ordering (fork opening → priming → leading extension → lagging fragment synthesis → maturation) is broadly consistent with the teaching model and the cited facts.",
    "Pol ε leading-strand label is appropriately hedged as the common model; no claim of absolute exclusivity is made. Keep that hedge in captions.",
    "The declared simplification allows omitting RNase H/FEN1 details; do not demand those steps, but the Pol α/primase distinction and nick adjacency should still be corrected.",
    "Because a blocker remains, scientific PASS is not permitted."
  ]
}
